lesson_title: A Tower Over a Hole in the Ground
hook_text: Look at any mining town's skyline. Those steel towers are the term's project, and your team is bidding to build one.
clip_script: A platinum mine near Rustenburg is sinking a shaft 800 metres to the reef. It needs a headgear: the tower over the shaft that lifts cages of miners and skips of rock. It has put out a tender, and your team is an engineering company bidding for it. The rope runs from a drum in the winder house, up over the big sheave wheel at the top, and down the shaft. So the headgear is two things: a braced structure that must not topple, and a mechanism, a motor turning a drum through gears that slow the speed and multiply the force. The term's map: three weeks of gears, three weeks of research and design, two weeks of budget and building, then the tender board. Model, drawings, calculations, budget, honesty. The board picks one.
visual_style: Whiteboard skyline with an A-frame headgear; a rope animates from drum to sheave to cage; the frame highlights as structure, the drum and gears as mechanism; a ten-week timeline unrolls beneath.
pacing: The notice, the rope's path, structure plus mechanism, the term map.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and name your engineering company before next week.
